question.problem: Given the inequalities $x < 3$ and $x \leq -1$, express their common set of solutions as an interval.
question.worked_solution:
We start by sketching the solutions to the two inequalities separately:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/166ce99c0ceedf97d38066b544b5dc6ff7ca63296572d952536193a83a410d94.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/7ff88166ac6f9e631cf8928e91c1c299986893051013f15387e153ecf4237866.png)

The common set of values consists of the values that are in both intervals. So, it can be graphed by finding where the two intervals overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/a77508881158e793810249877b3941fe52ae9e04056813d2222daae4aa0d5e50.png)

Therefore, the common set of values is
${\color{blue}(-\infty, -1]}.$
